To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
nearly 2/3 of all hippocampally-recorded pyramidal neurons are silent in freely-behaving rats and that these silent cells can become active in the presence of a barbiturate anesthetic.
the majority of the hippocampus is silent in the awake, behaving rat, and that place cells are not the majority of the neurons in this region.
nearly two-thirds of hippocampal pyramids are behaviorally silent and the remainder are place cells.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the neural basis of spatial memory in rats.
the relationship between the neural activity of individual neurons, their firing patterns, and the behavior of the animal in which they are located.
the neural mechanisms of spatial memory and the hippocampus.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the hippocampus is composed of two distinct populations of pyramidal cells: (1) place cells that fire in specific locations of the rat's environment and (2) silent cells that do not fire under normal conditions.
the majority of hippocampal pyramids are silent, and that the minority that are active, are place cells.
, under the present conditions, approximately 2/3 of the hippocampal pyramids are silent and the remaining 1/3 show place cell activity.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
, although most hippocampal pyramids are silent in freely-behaving rats, those that are not are spatially specific.
the silent cells are a major component of the pyramidal cell population of the rat hippocampus.
place cells and silent cells represent the two extremes of a continuum of spatial firing activity in the hippocampus.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the hippocampus contains many silent cells and many place cells.
the hippocampus, and perhaps other parts of the brain, may contain a much larger number of silent than active cells.
the hippocampal pyramids are a highly diverse population of cells, and that the diversity is not only in the firing patterns of these cells, but also in whether or not these cells fire spontaneously.
